messages.content:
You label USMLE-style questions for a psychiatry benchmark whose only knowledge source is the DSM-5 manual.

Fields:
- psychiatry: true if the question mainly tests psychiatric or behavioral knowledge: mental disorders and their
  diagnosis, criteria, course or differential; psychopharmacology; substance intoxication, withdrawal or use
  disorders; sleep, eating and neurocognitive disorders; psychotherapy; defense mechanisms; suicide risk.
  False when psychiatric words are incidental (e.g. "ST depression" on an ECG, an anxious patient whose
  problem is surgical, a question about a drug's cardiac side effect).
- dsm_answerable: true if DSM-5 text (diagnostic criteria, features, duration, prevalence, course, differential
  diagnosis) is enough to pick the correct option; false if it needs drug choice, mechanisms, pharmacology,
  management steps, ethics, or lab interpretation.
- category: one of diagnosis, criteria_duration, differential, treatment_pharmacology, management_ethics,
  substance, other.

Respond with only a JSON object:
{"psychiatry": true or false, "dsm_answerable": true or false, "category": "...", "reason": "one short sentence"}

Question:
A 57-year-old man comes to the physician because of a 3-month history of bloating and nausea after eating food. He has also had episodic abdominal pain during this period. He has osteoarthritis of the left knee. There is no family history of serious illness. He has smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for 21 years. He drinks two to three beers daily. Current medications include ibuprofen. He is allergic to amoxicillin and latex. Vital signs are within normal limits. The lungs are clear to auscultation. Cardiac examination shows no abnormalities. The abdomen is soft; there is mild tenderness to palpation over the epigastrium. Rectal examination shows no abnormalities. An esophagogastroduodenoscopy is performed and shows 3 shallow ulcers of the gastric mucosa. Biopsy shows chronic inflammation of the gastric mucosa and Helicobacter pylori. He is prescribed a 2-week course of antibiotics and omeprazole to treat the H. pylori infection. Which of the following recommendations is most appropriate at this time?

Options:
A. Avoid drinking alcohol for the next 2 weeks
B. Return for repeat endoscopy in 2 weeks
C. Begin prophylactic steroid therapy for anaphylaxis
D. Check liver enzymes in 2 weeks
E. Perform urea breath test in 2 weeks

Correct answer: A. Avoid drinking alcohol for the next 2 weeks

text: {"psychiatry": false, "dsm_answerable": false, "category": "other", "reason": "This is a gastroenterology question about H. pylori treatment and alcohol avoidance with antibiotics; the alcohol use detail is incidental and DSM-5 knowledge is irrelevant."}
